before: The first five season-three guides / numbered parts 1–6 have scoped reviews against 195 selected profiles, with 82 additive episode connections. Thirty-nine of 66 Rebels guides now have selected reviews; 27 guides / 32 numbered parts remain pending. The opener is a combined guide. Omitted links are unestablished, not absent.

Thrawn’s opener scenes are holographic transmissions; his Ryloth encounter is physical. Goran’s precise visible form and Hera’s final Agamar-related conversation remain unspecified. Original Phantom destruction and the recovered Phantom II stay separate, as do the RZ-1T trainer, generic A-wing and Sheathipede type/individual scopes.

Reklam’s salvaged Y-wings lack hyperdrives in that scene, without a universal Y-wing claim. Hobbie’s generic Biggs introduction conflicts with the released Wedge/Sabine-specific account; the discrepancy is explicit. Simulations, artwork, Legends origins and discarded outlines are not promoted to actual physical appearances.

Yoda’s remote Force contact, Anakin’s training recording plus vision, the Grand Inquisitor’s temple apparition and Vader’s separate physical arrival are explicitly distinguished. A combined guide never supplies unsourced per-part attribution.

Bahryn is a moon of Geonosis, the Lothal temple is distinct from Coruscant’s, and Malachor’s world and temple remain separate. Ketsu’s named participation has unspecified representation. Dicer has a sourced living scene before her disappearance; the finale’s closing Ahsoka image is retained without importing the later rescue.

Nixus Hub 218 has conflicting station/world descriptions across official trivia sources; this batch does not silently merge the current outpost with the existing station. Homecoming’s reinforcement is a light cruiser in the released narrative and Numa history but a Star Destroyer in Cham’s history; the discrepancy is visible and scoped.

Sato’s Homecoming appearance is a holographic transmission. Concord Dawn’s camp is on the third moon, separate from an unreviewed legacy planet. Lyste’s promotion retains one identity; Fang, Mining Guild fighters and the captured Quasar carrier do not inherit other hull or Legends specifications. Drawings, photos, memories and script-only labels are not promoted to living physical appearances.

Legacy parents are visions, Ryder and the tracked loth-cat have mixed vision/physical contexts, and Stealth Strike Kallus is a transmission. Blood Sisters names Bail at the rendezvous but the selected still does not establish physical versus holographic form; that row remains unspecified with a visible limitation.

The Blade Wing B6 prototype, GX1 starbus, Titus’s experimental Interdictor and Liberator remain distinct from production B-wings, old shuttles, generic/Legends models and the destroyed Phoenix Home. Chandel is a planned destination; Mustafar monitoring and decorative/design references do not establish visits.

Lando’s Siege hologram, the Emperor’s ending contact and Sato’s generator briefing are transmissions. Tua and Kallus retain direct rows when actual scenes accompany remote contact. Force sensing does not replace the actual physical scenes of Ahsoka, Kanan and Vader.

The modified Seelos walker, legacy AT-TE family, AT-AT family and distinct episode variant are scoped separately. The abandoned medical station shares a design with Kaliida Shoals but is not identified as that station. Nixus Hub 218, Tarkintown and the medical station are places, not additional planets. A single Ghost/Phantom caption inconsistency is explained, not copied into an unsupported ship location.

Trayvis’s vision, broadcast and physical meeting share one direct row with context. Alton/Trayvis interviews, Fulcrum’s remote conversation and Bail’s holographic greeting are transmissions. Ahsoka’s finale reveal and Vader’s Lothal arrival are direct scenes; later Kallus-Fulcrum biography is not assigned to the season-one contact.

The Sovereign, communications light-cruiser family, stolen rescue transport, Broken Horn and two distinct stolen/borrowed TIEs retain separate identities and scope. Mustafar is only a planned destination in Rebel Resolve but a system setting in the finale. No Gideon/Trask hull, generic Lambda, A-wing or technical metadata inferred.

Path of the Jedi distinguishes nightmare visions from direct scenes and Yoda’s remote communication through the Force. Mixed direct/vision contexts use one direct row with explanation; no real crew deaths or physical Yoda temple visit are asserted.

Fort Anaxes is the Rebels-era asteroid base. The displayed parade TIE and Inquisitor’s pursuit fighter are distinct. The Relentless has no assumed subclass and the landing shuttle has no assumed Lambda/Theta identity. No legacy technical fields inherited.

The combined Spark of Rebellion guide remains one review for parts 1–2. The later ABC Vader opening is excluded from original-pilot connections and remains a distinct documented version. No scene is assigned to an individual pilot part without evidence.

Obi-Wan’s holocron message, Trayvis’s broadcast and Luminara’s projected bait are transmissions. Luminara’s remains are also shown. Remote contacts followed by physical scenes use a single direct row with context; mentions, aliases and repeated names are not extra characters.
Episode inventory and writing credits do not establish every language mix, supplied master or frame-level version. Public references are not open media licences.
